title: A Novel Sensing Method to Detect Malachite Green Contaminant on Silicon Substrate Using Nonlinear Optics
description:
We propose a nonlinear-optics-based nanosensor to detect malachite green (MG) contaminants on semiconductor interfaces such as silicon (Si). Applying the simplified bond hyperpolarizability model (SBHM), we simplified the second-harmonic generation (SHG) analysis of an MG-Si(111) surface and were able to validate our model by reproducing experimental rotational anisotropy (RA) SHG experiments. For the first time, density functional theory (DFT) calculations using ultrasoft pseudopotentials were implemented to obtain the molecular configuration and bond vector orientation required by the SBHM to investigate and predict the second-harmonic generation contribution for an MG-Si 001 surface. We show that the SBHM model significantly reduces the number of independent components in the nonlinear tensor of the MG-Si(111) interface, opening up the possibility for real-time and non-destructive contaminant detection at the nanoscale. In addition, we derive an explicit formula for the SHG far field, demonstrating its applicability for various input polarization angles. Finally, an RASHG signal can be enhanced through a simulated photonic crystal cavity up to 4000 times for more sensitivity of detection. Our work can stimulate more exploration using nonlinear optical methods to detect and analyze surface-bound contaminants, which is beneficial for environmental monitoring, especially for mitigating pollution from textile dyes, and underscores the role of nonlinear optics in real-time ambient-condition applications.

title: Third-harmonic generation in tetragonal methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) perovskite
description:
Methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) is a key candidate for metal halide perovskite (MHP) solar cells due to its phase-dependent behavior and intriguing optoelectronic properties. Second-harmonic generation (SHG) is commonly employed to study their surface properties at the nanoscale. Meanwhile, third-harmonic generation (THG) allows unique, to the best of our knowledge, access to bulk properties even if the material is centrosymmetric. However, THG in perovskites has so far never been studied within the framework of the nonlinear bond model. Therefore, in this work, we develop the simplified bond-hyperpolarizability model (SBHM) to analyze THG in tetragonal  at the surface and bulk. To validate the bond model assumption that THG radiation is emitted with the oscillatory motion of bonds in covalent structures, we apply density functional theory to visualize the charge density of tetragonal . We further introduce effective bond hyperpolarizability, termed  in THG, to simplify the otherwise complex nonlinear optical interaction and study the fourth-rank tensor irreducible elements and predict the rotational anisotropy third-harmonic generation experiment. Using the SBHM, we show that MHP characterization at the bulk becomes simpler and more accessible through THG and, when combined with SHG, can produce a heuristic understanding of the nonlinear processes that shape the rotational anisotropy data. Our results broaden the scope for high-efficient design of solar cells through better understanding of real-time surface monitoring at the nanoscale, defect detection, and surface reconstruction in MHPs.

title: Recent Advances of Bond-Model-Based Nonlinear Photonic Sensors for Surface and Molecular Detection
description:
Nonlinear harmonic generation has transformed from a symmetry-selective spectroscopic method into a robust platform for surface-sensitive photonic sensing. This review focuses on recent progress in bond-model-based nonlinear photonic sensors, particularly the Simplified Bond Hyperpolarizability Model (SBHM), which provides a physically transparent framework connecting microscopic bond configurations to macroscopic secondharmonic generation (SHG) and third-harmonic generation (THG) responses. We describe how phenomenological tensor-based methods can be modified into bond-resolved models. These models make it possible to interpret polarization-resolved and rotationalanisotropy (RA) measurements in a way that is consistent with symmetry and uses fewer parameters.We look at how these ideas can be used in semiconductor interfaces, strained and oxidized silicon, doped ultrathin films, perovskites, layered materials, and molecular adsorption systems to detect organic contaminants. These advancements illustrate that bond-resolved harmonic generation offers an interpretable, scalable, and quantitatively robust methodology for next-generation surface and molecular photonic sensors.
https://doi.org/10.1142/S0218863526300021
